narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist; explains Jewish customs and Aramaic words to his readers.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Sharp with the hypocrites, patient teacher with the disciples, testing then granting the woman's plea.

pharisees-and-scribes.name: The Pharisees and Scribes
pharisees-and-scribes.note: Religious authorities from Jerusalem; fault-finding and accusing.

syrophoenician-woman.name: The Syrophoenician woman
syrophoenician-woman.note: A Gentile mother begging for her possessed daughter; humble and quick-witted.

crowd.name: The crowd in Decapolis
crowd.note: Witnesses of the healing of the deaf-mute; overflowing with wonder.

1.t: And there assembled together unto him the Pharisees, and some of the Scribes, coming from Jerusalem.

2.t: And when they had seen some of his disciples eat bread with common, that is, with unwashed, hands, they found fault.

3.t: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews eat not without often washing their hands, holding the tradition of the ancients:

4.t: And when they come from the market, unless they be washed, they eat not: and many other things there are that have been delivered to them to observe, the washings of cups, and of pots, and of brazen vessels, and of beds.

5.t: And the Pharisees and Scribes asked him:
Why do not thy disciples walk according to the tradition of the ancients, but they eat bread with common hands?

6.t: But he answering, said to them:
Well did Isaias prophesy of you, hypocrites, as it is written: This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

7.t: And in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and precepts of men.

8.t: For leaving the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men, the washing of pots, and of cups: and many other things you do like to these.

9.t: Well do you make void the commandment of God, that you may keep your own tradition.

10.t: For Moses said: Honour thy father and thy mother: and he that shall curse father or mother, let him die the death.

11.t: But you say: If a man shall say to his father or mother, Corban, (that is a gift,) whatsoever is from me, shall profit thee:

12.t: And farther you suffer him not to do any thing for his father or his mother,

13.t: Making void the word of God by your tradition, which you have given forth. And many other such like things you do.

14.t: And calling again the multitude unto him, he said to them:
Hear ye me all, and understand.

15.t: There is nothing from without a man entering into him, that can defile him: but the things which come from a man, those are they that defile a man.

16.t: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

17.t: And when he was come into the house from the multitude, his disciples asked him the parable.

18.t: Are you also so unwise? understand you not that whatever thing from without entering into a man, it cannot defile him:

19.t: Because it entereth not into his heart, but goeth into the belly, and goeth out into the privy, purging all meats?

20.t: the things which come out from a man, they defile a man.
20.q: indirect report ("he said that") which runs straight into direct speech in v21-23; the saying itself given to Jesus

21.t: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

22.t: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.

23.t: All these evil things come from within, and defile a man.

24.t: And rising from thence, he went to the borders of Tyre and Sidon: and entering into a house, he would no man know it, but he could not be hid.

25.t: For a certain woman heard of him, whose daughter had an unclean spirit, and presently came in, and fell down at his feet.

26.t: For the woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician born. And she besought him to cast forth the devil out of her daughter.

27.t: Let the children first be filled: for it is not good to take the bread of the children, and cast it to the dogs.

28.t: But she answered and said to him:
Yea, Lord; for the whelps also eat under the table of the crumbs of the children.

29.t: For this saying, go thy way, the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

30.t: And when she was come into her house, she found the girl lying upon the bed, and that the devil was gone out.

31.t: And again going out of the borders of Tyre, he came to Sidon to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.

32.t: And they bring to him one that was deaf and dumb, and they besought him to lay his hand upon him.

33.t: And taking him aside from the multitude, he put his fingers into his ears, and spitting, he touched his tongue:

34.t: And looking up to heaven, he groaned, and said to him,

34.q: the evangelist's translation gloss given to narrator; only the Aramaic word is Jesus

35.t: And immediately his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke right.

36.t: And he charged them that they should tell no man. But the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal did they publish it:

37.t: And so much the more did they wonder, saying,
He hath done all things well; he hath made both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
